text: so uh lets say i have some crazy 60mb model does that mean i can only load one in at a time or i can load maybe many in at a time it just would not be able to import all at once
resolution: User asked whether a ~60MB model means one-at-a-time loading or whether many can coexist (just not imported all at once). Answer: many. Verified the persistence topology — Studio models do NOT use the localstore KV value at all; they persist through the editor workspace store (editors/store.ts → editorChannel → ../data) into a per-domain on-disk SQLite + JSON-snapshot store (cart/hmsc-int/data/domains/model/), bounded by disk, not by the 4MB/64MB localstore MAX_VALUE (that ceiling, raised in req_2079, governs the world editor-state and game-state blobs only). A 60MB source file is also never stored at 60MB: import decimates to the chosen Detail (≤150k tris) and normalizes, so the stored EditMesh is far smaller. Each model is its own record in the model domain's models map, so many models accumulate on disk; the genuine limit is editor responsiveness (every face is a JS object edited/painted/undone), not storage, and only the import ACTION is one-file-at-a-time (the parse+decimate spike is now small and bounded). Also fixed a bug surfaced live during this investigation: GLB import threw 'TextDecoder is not defined' because the rewrite used new TextDecoder(), which exists in the v8cli build host but not the cart runtime — swapped to the shared in-cart bytesText() (sha b07c1ab6c).
